_comment: Custom-API customs gateway configuration.
This file is world-readable, so it must NOT contain secrets. Provider keys
and user tokens are supplied through the --env-file (see customsd.env.example):
CUSTOMS_PROVIDER_<PROVIDER>_APIKEY                  single-key provider
CUSTOMS_PROVIDER_<PROVIDER>_KEY_<KEYNAME>_APIKEY    one of several keys
CUSTOMS_PROVIDER_<PROVIDER>_BASEURL                 override the base URL
CUSTOMS_USER_<USERNAME>_TOKEN                        gateway client token
CUSTOMS_SERVER_<FIELD>                               listen, log_level, ...
A 'provider' is one vendor plus its API keys. Each enabled key becomes its
own routable channel named '<provider>' (one key) or '<provider>/<key>'
(several keys). That is what makes per-key failover work: a key that 429s or
500s is simply one unhealthy channel and the router moves to the next.
Three protocols are served natively:
/v1/chat/completions   OpenAI Chat Completions   protocol "openai"
/v1/responses          OpenAI Responses API      protocol "responses"
/v1/messages           Anthropic Messages        protocol "anthropic"
routing.prefer_same_protocol keeps the common path lossless: a channel that
already speaks the client's protocol always wins over one needing a
conversion. routing.allow_translation permits the conversion as a fallback,
and a provider receives a foreign protocol only if it declares it in
'supports' - so a chat-only endpoint is never handed a Responses request.
Unknown fields are rejected by design, so a misspelled key is a startup error
rather than a silently ignored default. Prose belongs here.
server.listen binds the user-facing API to every interface, because the point
of deploying this gateway is to let clients reach it. server.admin_listen
stays on loopback by default: the admin API can issue quota and read the
audit ledger, so reach it through an SSH tunnel rather than exposing it.
Prefer that. Exposing the listener is the second-best option, not the
first:
To reach the console from another machine, set admin_remote true AND
admin_token (in the 0640 env file, not here). Without the token the
listener answers 403 to every remote caller; with it, every remote call
must present it. The console's static shell stays reachable so the page
that asks for the token can load; the data behind /admin/* does not.
policy.metering: a usage deviation is reported only when it exceeds BOTH the
relative tolerance and the absolute floor. The floor is not optional: on a
five-token reply a three-token difference is +60%, so a purely relative rule
flags honest upstreams on exactly the short requests that health checks and
benchmark probes make.
This template ships with three aggregators, each holding one key named
"main", and both of them serving the same two models under the "openai"
(chat completions) and "responses" protocol surfaces. Because both are
declared in 'supports', neither model needs translation: a /v1/responses
request goes upstream as a Responses request.
The keys are deliberately absent from this file. Put them in the env file
as shown in customsd.env.example, then confirm with:
customsctl config check --config /usr/local/etc/customapi/customs.json
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8081/admin/providers | jq '.providers[] | {name, has_key: .keys[0].has_key}'
prices[] rows are keyed per channel+model and ship at zero. Zero means
"no price recorded", not "free": cost fields stay empty and the cheapest
strategy has nothing to rank on until real prices are filled in.
